verdict.rationale: Unleash documents per-environment flag configurations, so a flag can be enabled in development or test without enabling it in production. Backend API tokens are scoped to a single environment, which keeps a test client from reaching production configuration. The environments share one instance and the same flag definitions, so this is configuration isolation rather than a fully isolated sandbox account with separate data. missing for 10: a dedicated sandbox instance or account isolated from production data, documentation of seeding or resetting sandbox data, and independent or hands-on confirmation of test-versus-production isolation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: each environment has different feature flag configurations. This allows you to enable a flag in development or test without enabling it in production.
Environments represent different stages in your development lifecycle. They allow you to manage your product releases from local development to production.
Backend tokens are scoped to one or more projects and a single environment.
